title_en: Yuan Zhaohui v. Changjiang Real Estate (Hunan) Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over compulsory share acquisition
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 74 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, a shareholder who voted against a resolution of the shareholders' meeting to transfer the principal assets of the company is entitled to request the company to repurchase its equity at a reasonable price. Where a shareholder failed to attend the shareholders' meeting not due to its own fault, and although it did not vote against the shareholders' resolution, it expressly raised objections to the company's transfer of principal assets, the court shall support its request for the company to acquire its equity at a fair price.

full_text_en:
Yuan Zhaohui v. Changjiang Real Estate (Hunan) Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over company's acquisition of shares

[Ruling Summary]

Under Article 74 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, a shareholder who votes against a shareholders' resolution to transfer the company's main assets is entitled to request the company to repurchase its equity at a reasonable price. If a shareholder, through no fault of its own, fails to attend the shareholders' meeting and thus does not vote against the shareholders' resolution, but has clearly expressed opposition to the transfer of the company's main assets, the court shall support its request for the company to acquire its equity at a fair price.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2014) Min Shen Zi No. 2154

Applicant for Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Changjiang Real Estate (Hunan) Development Co., Ltd. Domicile: Building F, No. 208 Yinpen South Road, Yuelu District, Changsha City, Hunan Province.

Legal Representative: Shen Liang, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Luo Sheng, employee of the company.

Agent ad litem: Guo Caihong, employee of the company.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Yuan Zhaohui, male, Han ethnicity, born on April 15, 1968, residing in Changsha City, Hunan Province.

Agent ad litem: Zhong Ming, lawyer of Beijing Zhonglun Wende Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Yuan Xiao, lawyer of Hunan Yuanduan Law Firm.

The applicant for retrial, Changjiang Real Estate (Hunan) Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Changjiang Real Estate Company), due to a dispute with the respondent Yuan Zhaohui over the company's acquisition of shares, refused to accept the civil judgment (2013) Xiang Gao Fa Min Er Zhong Zi No. 91 of the Hunan High People's Court, and applied to this Court for retrial. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel to review this case, and the review has now been concluded.

The Changjiang Real Estate Company applied for retrial, alleging: First, the Changjiang Real Estate Company submitted six sets of new evidence, including the "Minutes of the 4th Shareholders' Meeting in 2009", the "Resolution of the Extraordinary Shareholders' Meeting in 2010", and the "Explanation" issued by the public security authority, sufficient to overturn the original judgment. Second, the original judgment found that Yuan Zhaohui had the right to request the Changjiang Real Estate Company to repurchase equity, and determined the share price based on the "Audit Report", lacking proof. Third, the "Certificates" issued by the former financial personnel of the Changjiang Real Estate Company, Yang Kai, Liu Dan, and Yan Shujun, submitted by Yuan Zhaohui, were forged and should not be used as the basis for finding facts. Fourth, the evidence materials submitted by Yuan Zhaohui after the expiration of the time limit were not subject to cross-examination, and the court should not have admitted them. Fifth, the financial files of the Changjiang Real Estate Company were subject to preservation measures by the court, and the Changjiang Real Estate Company was unable to collect them on its own. It submitted a written application to the court for investigation and collection, but the court erred in not investigating and collecting. Sixth, the original judgment applied Article 75 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Company Law") (Article 74 after the 2013 revision, hereinafter uniformly expressed as "Article 74"), finding that Yuan Zhaohui had the right to exercise the right to request share repurchase, which was an error in the application of law. Seventh, the judge at first instance in this case had illegal circumstances, should have withdrawn but did not. Eighth, Shen Liang and Zhong Jiguang, as co-owners of the company's property, should have participated in the proceedings but did not. Ninth, Yuan Zhaohui's claim was: to request a judgment that the Changjiang Real Estate Company acquire 20% of Yuan Zhaohui's equity in accordance with the Company Law. The judgment at second instance found that Yuan Zhaohui's request complied with the Company Law and the company's Articles of Association, exceeding Yuan Zhaohui's claim. The Changjiang Real Estate Company applied for retrial based on Items 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 11 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Yuan Zhaohui submitted a defense opinion that the retrial application of the Changjiang Real Estate Company lacked factual and legal basis and should be dismissed.

This Court holds: I. Regarding whether Yuan Zhaohui is entitled to request the Changjiang Real Estate Company to repurchase equity. On March 5, 2010, the Changjiang Real Estate Company formed a shareholders' resolution, specifying that the three shareholders Shen Liang, Zhong Jiguang, and Yuan Zhaohui jointly preside over the work, confirming that all financial revenues and expenditures, business activities and expenses, and external economic actions must go through declaration and be jointly signed and approved by all shareholders before execution, and requiring approval by shareholders' resolution for major asset transfers. However, according to the correspondence between the Changjiang Real Estate Company and Yuan Zhaohui, after the implementation of the joint approval office system, the Changjiang Real Estate Company sold the second-phase assets involved in the case. The transfer of these assets, from pricing to transfer, was not approved by shareholder Yuan Zhaohui, nor was he notified to attend the shareholders' meeting. Under Article 74 of the Company Law, a shareholder who votes against a shareholders' resolution to transfer the company's main assets is entitled to request the company to repurchase its equity at a reasonable price. In this case, formally, Yuan Zhaohui did not attend the shareholders' meeting and did not express objection to the shareholders' resolution by voting against it. However, the legislative intent of Article 74 of the Company Law is to protect the lawful rights and interests of dissenting shareholders. The provision on voting against is intended to require the dissenting shareholder to express its opposition to other shareholders. In this case, Yuan Zhaohui was not notified to attend the shareholders' meeting and had no way of knowing the shareholders' resolution and voted against it. Moreover, when Yuan Zhaohui applied to hold an extraordinary shareholders' meeting on August 19, 2010, he clearly expressed opposition to the transfer of the second-phase assets and demanded an immediate stop to the transfer of the said assets. The Changjiang Real Estate Company rejected Yuan Zhaohui's application and continued to transfer the second-phase assets, which had infringed upon Yuan Zhaohui's shareholder rights. Therefore, the court of second instance, in accordance with Article 74 of the Company Law, found that Yuan Zhaohui had the right to request the Changjiang Real Estate Company to acquire its equity at a fair price, which was not improper.

At the same time, the "Articles of Association" of the Changjiang Real Estate Company stipulates that if a shareholder's rights are infringed by the company, the shareholder may request the company in writing to cease the infringing activities within a specified period and compensate for the economic losses caused by the infringement. If the company is confirmed by the court or the company registration authority that the company did not cease the infringing activities within the required period, the infringed shareholder may withdraw from the company according to its own wishes, and its shares shall be apportioned by agreement among other shareholders or subscribed by other shareholders in proportion to their shareholdings. In this case, without notifying Yuan Zhaohui to participate in the shareholders' meeting, the Changjiang Real Estate Company passed a shareholders' resolution on May 31, 2010, canceling all of Yuan Zhaohui's expenses. The Changjiang Real Estate Company and its shareholders' meeting did not safeguard Yuan Zhaohui's decision-making rights and information rights as a shareholder, infringing Yuan Zhaohui's shareholder rights, which falls under the circumstance of "shareholder's rights infringed by the company" as stipulated in the "Articles of Association" of the Changjiang Real Estate Company. Therefore, Yuan Zhaohui is entitled to request the company to allow him to withdraw from the company by way of equity repurchase in accordance with the provisions of the "Articles of Association".

From the actual effect of handling this case, the shareholders of the Changjiang Real Estate Company have had multiple lawsuits due to interest disputes, and the human relations nature of the limited liability company no longer exists. Allowing shareholder Yuan Zhaohui to withdraw from the company is conducive to quickly resolving the contradictions and conflicts among the company's shareholders, thereby safeguarding the interests of the company and its shareholders. If the Changjiang Real Estate Company has evidence that Yuan Zhaohui has misappropriated company assets, it may file a separate claim. In summary, Yuan Zhaohui's request for the Changjiang Real Estate Company to acquire its 20% equity complies with the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the "Articles of Association" of the Changjiang Real Estate Company. The evidence materials submitted by the Changjiang Real Estate Company, including the "Minutes of the 4th Shareholders' Meeting in 2009", the "Resolution of the Extraordinary Shareholders' Meeting in 2010", the "Explanation" issued by the Economic Crime Investigation Brigade of Yuelu Sub-bureau of Changsha Public Security Bureau, the "Civil Ruling" (2014) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 29 of the Hunan High People's Court, and the correspondence between shareholders Zhong Jiguang and Shen Liang, cannot constitute new evidence sufficient to overturn the judgment of the second instance. This Court does not admit them.

II. Regarding how the repurchase price of the equity should be determined. The Changjiang Real Estate Company submitted nine sets of evidence in the second instance, purporting to prove that the conclusion on the net assets of the Changjiang Real Estate Company in the "Audit Report" could be adjusted accordingly. The court of second instance organized the parties to cross-examine these nine sets of evidence. Upon review, the amounts proved by the above evidence have all been included in the scope of the audit and cannot achieve the purpose that the Changjiang Real Estate Company intended to prove. They do not fall under the circumstance in Item 5 of the "Audit Report" that "if new evidence or materials appear, after being verified through judicial proceedings by the court, the audit results may be adjusted accordingly."

III. Regarding whether there was a circumstance in this case where a trial judge should have withdrawn but did not. After verification with the parties, the situation claimed by the Changjiang Real Estate Company that a trial judge met with a party in violation of regulations was actually a scene recorded by the employees of the Changjiang Real Estate Company using monitoring equipment when the trial judge of the court of first instance organized the parties to investigate and collect evidence at the premises of the Changjiang Real Estate Company. There was no situation where the trial judge privately met with one party. The Changjiang Real Estate Company has no evidence that the trial judge had other circumstances requiring withdrawal as provided by law. The court of first instance did not err in not granting its withdrawal application.

IV. Regarding whether the main evidence for finding the facts in this case was not cross-examined. During the trial at first instance, to ascertain the facts of the case, after the expiration of the time limit for adducing evidence, the court of first instance requested Yuan Zhaohui to continue to provide relevant supplementary evidence on the basis of the original evidence to prove the equity value. Pursuant to Article 1 of the "Notice on the Application of the Provisions on the Time Limit for Adducing Evidence in the Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings" of the Supreme People's Court, after the expiration of the time limit for adducing evidence, for a specific fact or specific evidence or for specific reasons, the people's court may, based on the specific circumstances of the case, specify an appropriate time limit for the parties to adduce evidence or counter-evidence, which time limit is not subject to the restriction of "not less than thirty days". The court of first instance organized cross-examination for all evidence submitted by both parties. The failure of the Changjiang Real Estate Company to cross-examine relevant evidence constitutes a waiver of its litigation rights and does not affect the validity of the evidence having been cross-examined in court.

V. Regarding whether the court of original trial should have collected evidence but failed to do so. Both parties submitted multiple pieces of evidence to the court, all of which were received and cross-examined. For the purpose of hearing the case, the court of first instance obtained all sales materials of the project involved in the case from the Changsha Real Estate Information Center, obtained financial materials from the Changjiang Real Estate Company together with the parties and the audit department, and distinguished and compared the above evidence, incorporating it into the scope of the audit. The Changjiang Real Estate Company's application in the second instance for the court to collect evidence that had already been preserved lacks basis, and the court of second instance did not err in not granting it.

VI. Regarding whether the original judgment exceeded Yuan Zhaohui's claims. Yuan Zhaohui requested in his complaint that the Changjiang Real Estate Company repurchase its 20% equity, and the court of first instance also rendered a judgment ordering the Changjiang Real Estate Company to repurchase the said equity at a reasonable price, which did not exceed the claims. Whether the basis for the judgment is the provisions of the Company Law or the "Articles of Association" is the basis for the judgment, not the claim. Moreover, Yuan Zhaohui clearly stated in the main body of the complaint that he filed the claim based on Article 74 of the Company Law and the provisions of the "Articles of Association", not solely based on the Company Law. This Court does not support the Changjiang Real Estate Company's argument that the original judgment exceeded the claims.

VII. Regarding whether Zhong Jiguang and Shen Liang should participate in the proceedings. This case is an action in which a dissenting shareholder negotiates with the company and, failing agreement, requests the company to allow withdrawal. The plaintiff and defendant are clear. Other shareholders have neither an independent claim nor a legal interest in the equity held by the dissenting shareholder and are not necessary parties to the proceedings. The court of original trial did not err in not adding them.

As for the Changjiang Real Estate Company's claim that the court of first instance improperly suspended the proceedings and extended the trial period, there is no evidence to support it, and it does not fall under the grounds for retrial provided in the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. This Court does not support it.

In summary, the retrial application of the Changjiang Real Estate Company does not meet the circumstances provided in Items 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 11 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. In accordance with Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court rules as follows:

The retrial application of Changjiang Real Estate (Hunan) Development Co., Ltd. is dismissed.

Presiding Judge: Zhang Yongjian

Judge: Li Jingping

Acting Judge: Jin Lijuan

October 29, 2015

Clerk: Chen Ming

[Introduction to the Presiding Judge]

Senior Judge Zhang Yongjian: born in 1958, Master of Laws, appointed as Judge of the Supreme People's Court in 2005.
